standard-errors BeginSignInController: OAuth endpoint. Its 400s are documented individually because what they mean is specific (an unregistered redirect_uri is deliberately not a redirect), and there is no 404: the route takes no resource id.
standard-errors CompleteSignInController: OAuth endpoint. Its one 400 (no pending sign-in for that state) is documented on the operation; there is no resource to 404 on.
standard-errors CreateTokenController: RFC 6749 §5.2 defines the error body as { error, error_description }, which is not this API's standard error shape. Documenting the standard one here would describe a response the endpoint must never send.
standard-errors DescribeCurrentUserContr: No path parameter and no body, so neither a 400 nor a 404 is reachable. It documents the 401 it can actually answer instead. The convention is written for resource endpoints.
standard-errors ListSessionsController: No path parameter and no body, so neither a 400 nor a 404 is reachable. It documents the 401 it can actually answer instead.
success-response BeginSignInController: Answers only 302, to the identity provider. There is no 2xx it can send.
success-response CompleteSignInControlle: Answers only 302, back to the client — with a code or with error=access_denied. There is no 2xx it can send.
version DescribeJsonWebKeySetController: /.well-known/jwks.json is fixed by RFC 8615 and RFC 7517: a client looking for a key set looks there and nowhere else, so the path cannot carry /v1.
